instruction:
GUI-only requirement: Complete the entire task through the launched graphical user interfaces only. Do not open Terminal, Command Prompt, PowerShell, or any shell. Do not run Python, VBA, macros, Abaqus noGUI, ANSYS command scripts, batch/headless tools, APIs, or helper code that directly generates or edits the deliverable files. Use only the native SolidWorks and Abaqus/CAE GUI tools, menus, dialogs, editors, and built-in import, export, save, submit, and solve commands.

Two-software CAE flow: SolidWorks -> Abaqus/CAE. No init file is provided; start from a new blank SolidWorks part.

Chain evidence requirement: use the design token EW_SW_ABQ_08. Keep this token encoded in the SolidWorks part/custom properties or STEP export metadata so the text of stage1_geometry.step contains EW_SW_ABQ_08 and SOLIDWORKS_TO_ABAQUS. In Abaqus/CAE, create at least one model, part, instance, set, surface, job description, or other native name containing both EW_SW_ABQ_08 and IMPORTED_FROM_stage1_geometry.step, so the final CAE file carries evidence that Abaqus consumed the SolidWorks STEP handoff.


1. In SolidWorks, use GUI sketch and feature tools only to create a 100 mm x 50 mm x 5 mm base heat spreader with two 5 mm thick side walls rising to about 25 mm total height and a flat bottom heat-pad face. Export the completed CAD geometry to C:\Users\user\Desktop\stage1_geometry.step.
2. In Abaqus/CAE, import stage1_geometry.step through the GUI and create the finite-element model. Use the model name Model-UChannelThermal. Define material Aluminum with conductivity about 170 W/m-K, create a section using Aluminum, and assign it to the U-channel. Create a steady heat transfer step named Step-Thermal. Create a set named HEAT_PAD and a surface named CONVECTION_SURFACES. Use first-order heat-transfer elements such as DC3D8 where practical or coarse DC3D4 where needed. Create a heat flux load named HeatFlux-Base on HEAT_PAD. Create a convection interaction or equivalent boundary condition named BC-Convection on CONVECTION_SURFACES. Submit the job named Job-UChannelThermal and wait for the analysis to complete.
3. Required deliverables on the Desktop: C:\Users\user\Desktop\stage1_geometry.step, C:\Users\user\Desktop\Job-UChannelThermal.cae, and C:\Users\user\Desktop\Job-UChannelThermal.odb. Do not create extra STEP, DXF, CAE, or ODB deliverables.

[Software] Open and use SolidWorks and Abaqus/CAE one at a time through the Windows GUI as needed. First use SolidWorks to create and export the CAD STEP file, then use Abaqus/CAE to import that STEP file, build the finite-element model, submit the job, and save the CAE and ODB deliverables.
